Mathematical Kinematics, Dynamics & Literature Reference Sheet
Department of Aerospace Engineering • Microgravity Simulation Laboratory

Random Positioning Machine (RPM): Mathematical Kinematics, Rigid-Body Dynamics, and Acceleration Field Formulations

Department of Aerospace Engineering • Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), Thiruvananthapuram

1. Kinematic Frame Transformations & Direction Cosine Matrices

Let $\mathcal{F}_{\text{lab}} = \{\vec{e}_X, \vec{e}_Y, \vec{e}_Z\}$ denote the stationary laboratory reference frame where static terrestrial gravity is $\vec{g}_0 = -g_0 \vec{e}_Z$ ($g_0 = 9.80665\text{ m/s}^2$). The outer gimbal frame rotates through angle $\psi$ about the horizontal laboratory shaft ($Y$-axis), and the inner gimbal rotates through angle $\phi$ about its orthogonal gimbal shaft ($Z$-axis). The instantaneous gravity unit vector projected into the payload frame $\mathcal{F}_{\text{payload}}$ is governed by sequential orthogonal rotation matrices:

$$\vec{e}_g(t) = R_Z(-\phi) R_Y(-\psi) \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -\sin\phi \cos\psi \\ \sin\phi \sin\psi \\ \cos\phi \end{bmatrix}$$

When gimbal axis inclination misalignment tilts ($\theta_{\text{inner}}, \theta_{\text{outer}}$) exist, the effective instantaneous orientation angles become $\phi' = \phi + \theta_{\text{inner}}$ and $\psi' = \psi + \theta_{\text{outer}}$.

2. Cumulative Time-Averaged Simulated Microgravity (taSMG)

The cumulative Time-Averaged Simulated Microgravity ($\text{taSMG}$) over an operational epoch $T$ is defined as the Euclidean $L_2$-norm of the integrated orientation vector:

$$\text{taSMG}(T) = \left\| \frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} \vec{e}_g(t) \, dt \right\|_2 = \sqrt{\langle g_x \rangle^2 + \langle g_y \rangle^2 + \langle g_z \rangle^2}$$

To achieve uniform spherical coverage across the unit sphere $S^2$ and avoid closed 1D Lissajous degenerate orbits, non-harmonic velocity ratios ($\gamma = \omega_\psi / \omega_\phi \notin \mathbb{Q}$) or zero-crossing stochastic trajectories are employed, suppressing directional gravity accumulation to $\langle \vec{g} \rangle \to \vec{0}$.

3. Instantaneous Volumetric Spatial Acceleration Field

At any spatial position vector $\vec{r} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to the central gimbal pivot, the total instantaneous kinematic acceleration experienced by a continuum element incorporates terrestrial gravity, centrifugal acceleration, and angular acceleration:

$$\vec{a}_{\text{total}}(\vec{r}, t) = \vec{g}(t) - \vec{\omega}(t) \times \left( \vec{\omega}(t) \times \vec{r} \right) - \vec{\alpha}(t) \times \vec{r}$$

The radial centrifugal acceleration magnitude depends directly on composite rotational velocity and radius:

$$a_c(r) = \|\vec{\omega}\|^2 r = \left( \omega_\psi^2 + \omega_\phi^2 \right) r$$

For microgravity compliance ($a_c \le 10^{-3} g_0$), the critical safe radius threshold is defined by:

$$r_{\text{crit}} = \frac{10^{-3} g_0}{\|\vec{\omega}\|^2}$$

4. Rigid-Body Mass Moments of Inertia & Material Density Scaling

The mass moment of inertia tensor $\mathbf{I}$ of each rotating gimbal is evaluated directly from volumetric mass integration:

$$I_{ij} = \int_{V} \rho(\mathbf{x}) \left( \|\mathbf{x}\|^2 \delta_{ij} - x_i x_j \right) dV$$

For square hollow structural tubes (outer frame $500 \times 500 \times 50.8\text{ mm}$, inner frame $350 \times 350 \times 50.8\text{ mm}$ with wall thickness $t = 3.2\text{ mm}$), the structural frame mass and principal inertia scale linearly with material density $\rho$:

$$M_{\text{frame}} = \rho \cdot \left[ w^2 - (w - 2t)^2 \right] \cdot 4(L - w), \qquad I_{yy} = I_{\text{inner}} + I_{\text{payload}}, \quad I_{xx} = I_{\text{outer}} + I_{yy}$$

Selecting Al6061-T6 ($\rho = 2700\text{ kg/m}^3$) yields $I_{xx} \approx 0.485\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$ and $I_{yy} \approx 0.172\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$, whereas Structural Steel IS2062 ($\rho = 7850\text{ kg/m}^3$) scales inertia by a factor of $2.91\times$.

5. Dynamic Motor Shaft Torque & Gyroscopic Cross-Coupling

The instantaneous dynamic torque required from each drive actuator is a non-linear function of angular velocity $\omega$, angular acceleration $\alpha$, gimbal angle, and material inertia:

$$\tau_{\text{motor}}(\omega, \alpha) = I \alpha + \tau_{\text{gyro}}(\omega) + M_{\text{payload}} g \Delta r_{\text{cg}} \sin\theta + \tau_{\text{drag}}(\omega)$$

Where gyroscopic precession cross-coupling between orthogonal gimbal rotations contributes:

$$\tau_{\text{gyro}} = I_{yy} \cdot \left| \omega_\psi \omega_\phi \sin\phi \right|$$

And speed-dependent drag combines Coulomb dry friction, bearing lubricant shear, and aerodynamic windage:

$$\tau_{\text{drag}}(\omega) = \tau_{\text{Coulomb}} + c_{\text{viscous}} |\omega| + c_{\text{aero}} \omega^2$$

6. Peer-Reviewed Literature References

  1. Borst, A. G., & van Loon, J. J. W. A. (2009): Technology and developments for the Random Positioning Machine, RPM. Microgravity Science and Technology, 21(4), 287–292.
  2. Mesland, D. A. M., Anton, A. H., & Willemsen, H. P. (1996): The Random Positioning Machine: A tool for microgravity research. ESA Special Publication, SP-390, 143–148.
  3. Wuest, S. L., Richard, S., Kopp, S., Grimm, D., & Egli, M. (2015): Simulated microgravity: critical review on the use of 2D/3D clinostats, random positioning machines and ground-based facilities. Life Sciences in Space Research, 5, 45–54.
  4. Yotov, V., et al. (2022): Kinematic analysis and trajectory optimization of dual-axis random positioning machines. Aerospace Science and Technology, 128, 107802.

Electromechanical Integration Overview
The IIST RPM employs a dual-gimbal nested rotation structure requiring continuous 360° unconstrained rotation across two orthogonal axes. Power, real-time closed-loop motor control, and synchronous multi-sensor DAQ telemetry are routed through two commercial 12-channel gold-on-gold slip ring capsules, isolating high-current motor power from microvolt-sensitive telemetry lines.
LEVEL 0: Stationary Base Frame & Ground Control 24V DC / 15A Bus
Power Subsystem: Mean Well LRS-350-24 Industrial Switch-Mode PSU (24V DC, 14.6A) with inline dual-channel Emergency Stop relay contactor and EMI line filter.
Master SBC: Raspberry Pi 5 (4× Cortex-A76 @ 2.4 GHz, PREEMPT_RT patched Linux kernel). Runs the 50 Hz trajectory planner, kinematics engine, and native WebSocket server.
Stationary Motor Driver: Trinamic TMC5160 SilentStepStick (SPI control + Step/Dir), driving stationary NEMA 23 stepper motor (2.8 N·m, 3.0A).
Position Feedback: 1000 CPR Optical Quadrature Encoder with line driver (A+, A-, B+, B-, Z+, Z-).
CAN 2.0B (500 kbps) WebSocket (ws://localhost:8080) 24V DC / 15A
▼ ROTATING JOINT 1: Stationary Base → Outer Gimbal (12-Channel Gold Capsule Slip Ring 1) ▼
LEVEL 1: Outer Rotating Gimbal Frame (500×500 mm Al6061-T6) Vertical Axis Motor
Gimbal Driver: Frame-mounted TMC5160 driver with passive extruded aluminum heatsink.
Vertical Motor: NEMA 23 High-Torque Bipolar Stepper (2.8 N·m) coupled to inner gimbal vertical shaft via zero-backlash spider coupling.
Index Sensor: Miniature Hall-effect optical homing switch for absolute zero-position calibration at startup.
CAN Node: MCP2562 transceiver for remote driver status telemetry and overtemperature monitoring.
▼ ROTATING JOINT 2: Outer Gimbal → Inner Gimbal (12-Channel Gold Capsule Slip Ring 2) ▼
LEVEL 2 & 3: Sealed Payload Chamber & Embedded DAQ (200×200 mm) 1 kHz Synchronous Sampling
Microcontroller: STM32F405RG (168 MHz Cortex-M4 with hardware FPU) or RP2040 running FreeRTOS with microsecond task scheduling.
Primary Center-of-Mass IMU: TDK InvenSense ICM-42688-P (Ultra-low noise 6-axis, ±3g full-scale, SPI @ 10 MHz, hardware FIFO sampled at 1 kHz).
Boundary Reference IMU: Bosch BMI088 (mounted at r = 10 cm on chamber wall to measure radial centrifugal gradient a_c(r)).
Chamber Pressure Transducer: Honeywell ABP Series 0–2 bar Absolute Pressure Transducer (I2C @ 400 kHz) for chamber atmosphere monitoring.
Thermal Probe: 4-wire PT100 RTD with MAX31865 24-bit SPI Converter (for melt pool / crucible thermal tracking).
Micro-Disconnection Ring Buffer: 32MB Winbond SPI NOR Flash (stores up to 2 hours of raw telemetry during transient slip-ring brush micro-interruptions < 5 ms).
Bus Interface: MCP2562 CAN transceiver with 120Ω termination, packaging frames (CAN ID 0x100 for IMU, 0x101 for Pressure/Temp).
SPI @ 10 MHz I2C @ 400 kHz CAN 2.0B (500 kbps) 32MB SPI Flash
